body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: clang++ 22.1.8 -m32 -O2 emits b0 01 c3 for the reconstruction, identical to the three bytes read live at 0x00b1fbf0. The thiscall spelling of the same body emits the same three bytes.

semantic_findings: The whole observable contract is 'return the byte 1'. There is no input, no state read and no side effect, so the function is a constant.

Because it is constant and takes nothing, the compiled bytes are identical under every x86-32 convention. The observed mixed usage, a thiscall-shaped virtual slot at 0x00ee8860 alongside fifteen direct sites that set up nothing, is exactly what a __thiscall member with no stack arguments produces.

The same address is stored at +0x10, +0x14 and +0x2c in three different tables. A single named interface method could not occupy three offsets, so this address is a shared folded default body rather than one method.

0x007f5403 carries an inlined duplicate of the identical body inside caller 0x007f53d0, two bytes after the JMP at 0x007f53fe that tail-transfers to it. A shipped header default that the compiler can inline but sometimes emits out of line is the shape that produces both.
Every inspected consumer treats the answer as a boolean predicate (TEST AL,AL), and two consumers discard it entirely, so the only role the evidence supports is 'unconditional yes'.
unresolved_questions: What predicate is this? The body is a constant yes, but nothing in the observed evidence names the question it answers.
Which class or classes own the slots that point here? Three distinct slot offsets across three distinct tables are recorded above and they cannot all describe one method.
Is the address a compiler-folded COMDAT shared by many unrelated 'return true' defaults, or a single default deliberately emitted once? Both fit every observation.
Is the always-true body a shipped default, a build-configuration stub, or a patch target at runtime? No differential trace has been captured for this function, so runtime patching cannot be excluded.
Why does caller 0x00a43050 and caller 0x0082c210 call the function and discard the answer? A constant with no side effects makes those calls no-ops in the observed build.

What is the correct port spelling for a slot that is dispatched with ECX populated but implemented as a bare RET? The reconstruction keeps an unread receiver parameter, which is a modelling choice rather than an observed fact.
The 356 and 20 vtable-reference counts are raw pointer-scan totals, not proven distinct vtables. The true count is unmeasured.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00b1fbf0, so every claim here is static. A runtime differential test must confirm that the answer is still 1 in the shipping build and that no runtime patch retargets the address.
The 0x00ee8860 virtual dispatch site must be observed with a concrete receiver before the slot's owning class can be named.
